 General Notes
  
 The Department of Physics plays a pivotal role in the advancing of knowledge, nurturing the next generation of physicists and making a lasting impact on the world of physics.

 For more details, please see: Prospective Employee Benefits and My Total Rewards . 

 Job Description Summary 

 The Center for High Energy Density Science (CHEDS) at The University of Texas at Austin seeks an accomplished experimental physicist to lead a program on laser wakefield electron accelerators, laser-driven x-ray sources, laser-driven muon sources, and the physics they enable. The successful candidate will build UT’s laser-based x-ray capability for semiconductor and medical applications, support the LaVHEE effort on laser-driven very-high-energy electron (VHEE) beams for radiotherapy, play a leading role in UT’s participation in the LSU-led LaNeXT project (The Laboratory for Next Generation X-ray Science and Technology, NSF Mid-scale RI-1), and lead the x-ray beamline portion of TeX-Ray, a planned Texas laser synchrotron facility, including support for its laser development.  
 The position offers a highly independent research role with the opportunity to lead proposals, supervise researchers and students, and shape a new national user facility, at the interface of ultra-high-intensity laser science, accelerator physics, semiconductor metrology and medical imaging.  
 


 Responsibilities 

 Lead the research program on laser wakefield electron accelerators and betatron, inverse-Compton and other laser-driven x-ray sources, including experiments on UT3, the Texas Petawatt (TPW) and off-site facilities (e.g., BELLA at LBNL, ELI Beamlines, ELI-NP). 
 Develop laser-based x-ray diagnostics for semiconductor and medical applications, including 3D micro-CT of packaged chips, x-ray diffraction (XRD), phase-contrast imaging and related techniques, and support the development of laser-driven VHEE beams for radiotherapy (LaVHEE), working with industry and clinical partners. 
 Lead the x-ray beamline portion of TeX-Ray (MIMIX and associated beamlines): beamline design, commissioning, and operation, and support laser development for the facility. 
 Take a leading role in UT’s participation in the LSU LaNeXT project: co-lead UT’s part of the proposal and project, represent UT with LSU and the partner institutions, define and deliver UT’s laser-driven x-ray contributions, and develop related user-program and funding efforts. 
 Publish results, present at conferences, and supervise postdoctoral researchers, graduate students, technical staff and undergraduate research assistants. 
 
Qualification s  

 Ph.D. in Physics, Applied Physics or a related field and a minimum of six years of post-Ph.D. experience, and at least eight years of total research experience (including pre-doctoral research at universities or national laboratories), in experimental laser-plasma physics or accelerator science.  
 Demonstrated record of leading experiments on laser wakefield acceleration and laser-driven x-ray generation (betatron, inverse Compton, or similar), documented by peer-reviewed publications.  
 Experience with x-ray imaging or scattering techniques (e.g., radiography, micro-CT, XRD, phase-contrast) including detectors, optics and data reconstruction.  
 Experience with high-power (≥ 50 TW) Ti:sapphire laser systems and with executing experiments at external laser facilities.  
 Record of securing external research funding or leading major proposal components (e.g., NSF mid-scale or multi-institution projects), and of supervising researchers and students.  
 
 Preferred Qualifications  

 Experience developing x-ray metrology for semiconductor or medical applications, or collaborations with industry or clinical partners.  
 Experience designing and commissioning beamlines or user end stations at a laser, synchrotron or accelerator facility.  
 Experience with high-repetition-rate laser-plasma systems, gas-jet and gas-cell targets, and electron and x-ray beam diagnostics.  
 Experience in muon physics, laser-based muon generation, and muon imaging (e.g., muon tomography).  
 Experience with ML/AI methods for data analysis, tomographic reconstruction or machine control.  
 Experience with PIC and x-ray transport simulation (e.g., WarpX, Osiris, Geant4) and with Python or C++.  
 
 Salary Range 
  $100,000 plus depending on qualifications.  

 Working Conditions  
 Work in an academic research environment and in laser laboratories  
 Repetitive use of a keyboard  
 Will work with UT3, the Texas Petawatt and associated laboratories at UT Austin, with Class IV lasers, high-voltage systems, vacuum systems and ionizing radiation (x-ray) sources  
 Travel to and work at offsite facilities (e.g., LBNL, ELI Beamlines, ELI-NP, LSU, national laboratories) and to meetings with partners  
 Required Materials  
 Curriculum Vitae (CV), including a list of publications  
 Statement of research interests  
 3 letters of reference, at least two of which must be from references outside The University of Texas at Austin.  
 
 Important for applicants who are NOT current university employees or contingent workers: You will be prompted to submit your resume in the first step of the online job application process. Then, any additional Required Materials will be uploaded in the My Experience section; you can multi-select the additional files or click the Upload button for each file. Before submitting your online job application, ensure that  ALL  Required Materials have been uploaded.  Once your job application has been submitted, you cannot make changes. 
 Important for Current university employees and contingent workers: As a current university employee or contingent worker, you MUST apply within Workday by searching for Find Jobs. Before you apply though, log-in to Workday, navigate to your Worker Profile, click the Career link in the left-hand navigation menu and then update the sections in your Professional Profile. This information will be pulled into your application. The application is one page, and you will need to click the Upload button multiple times in order to attach your Resume, References and any additional Required Materials noted above.

 Employment Eligibility: 
Regular staff who have been employed in their current position for the last six continuous months are eligible for openings being recruited for through University-Wide or Open Recruiting, to include both promotional opportunities and lateral transfers. Staff who are promotion/transfer eligible may apply for positions without supervisor approval. ----
 Retirement Plan Eligibility: 
The retirement plan for this position is Teacher Retirement System of Texas (TRS), subject to the position being at least 20 hours per week and at least 135 days in length. This position has the option to elect the Optional Retirement Program (ORP) instead of TRS, subject to the position being 40 hours per week and at least 135 days in length. ----
